Super fun game. The gameplay is punchy and fast, but I wish there was more content to the game. There's not a whole lot here and it'll drip feed you content over the next few months, which kinda sucks for a full priced game. But if you're as invested in MK as I am, you'll at least enjoy the story and the fighting.

The story doesn’t amount to much. As for the online game, 20% of the players are giving you a real beating and not giving you a chance. The remaining 80% are full of son of bitches who just keep spamming the L1 button and spamming useless long-range abilities, waiting for you to get right up close to them.

So it's official; this game is done. Two seasons in, and Warner Brothers are cutting their losses. I think it's time to revisit my thoughts on this one.

For context, I'm a long-time MK fan here. Just looking at the trailers - especially the Kameo mechanics and the story - you got the sense that this one was doomed. NetherRealm are touted as being the best FG developers in the business for single-player content, and I don't know how many of the decisions were theirs. But the story feels lazy, and that dungeon mode is boring as anything. Grindy, repetitive, and (worst of all) not fun. Which is a shame, because despite its flaws, the game plays decently.

There are more positives. The guest characters are easily the best in the franchise. Haters have a wealth of material to use against WB for this one, but not the DLC roster. Omni-Man? Sick. Peacemaker? Fitting. Ghostface? My personal favourite. In fact, the roster as a whole is real solid this time around. But it's an uphill battle when the modes on offer are as weak as they are.

This is a repetitive fighter, looking to extort the player of both time and money. And it is likely to be the last MK I ever buy.

Played it on day one. It was definitely something new, but after a while it started to feel a bit stale. I have around 100 hours in the game, and while I enjoyed it, nothing has come close to the peak that Mortal Kombat X on PS4 was for me.
This was my first Mortal Kombat on PC, and I managed to reach Grand Master. The online experience is great, and honestly, there isn't much more I could ask for from a Mortal Kombat game gameplay wise. My only major gripe is the Kameo system. If NetherRealm wanted to add tag team style gameplay, they already nailed it back in MK9. Kameos just feel unnecessary and gimmicky to me.
My biggest complaint was the game's size at launch. It was over 200 GB, which was absolutely insane. Thankfully, it's been reduced since then, but not by a huge amount.
Overall, Mortal Kombat 1 is a solid game, but at this point I'd only recommend picking it up during a major sale.
If you're stuck trying to figure out the fatality combo for your wallet it's: Add to Cart, Purchase For Myself, Agree to Terms + Purchase (Close distance).

This has to be the worst PC port I have ever played. WB should be ashamed that their flagship fighting game franchise can't load a character intro without stuttering. My settings are set to "Ultra Performance" and it is still the worst performing game I've played to date. Not even Arkham Origins, which crashes every thirty minutes, performs this bad. It's no wonder this game dropped off the face of the Earth after release. This is a pathetic excuse of a port. You should not buy this on PC if you can avoid it. And even if you can only buy it on PC, don't. You'll spend thirty minutes digging through various forums on how to get the game to be even remotely playable and any fight you have will still freeze in the character intro, finishing blow or fatality "cut-scenes." Awful. Just plain awful.

The game is fun, but there are SO many egregious flaws that are still present or even growing, from monetization to bugs that have no reason to still be present. As a not very competitive player, mostly just playing local or online with friends, some of the main issues lie in things like random moves/brutalities/fatalities somehow still have incorrect inputs displayed on the menus this long after launch, player 2 in local not being able to use any skins/items OR being able to see any unlocked fatality/brutality inputs (which is downright stupid). As far as monetization goes, you get a very finite number of premium currency which is whatever, I can look past not being able to get every skin, but the sheer number of what's being monetized is crazy. Even the upcoming seasonal Halloween fatality is going to be added to the premium store; a FATALITY will be pay-walled. Invasions mode is alright IMO and I like the seasonal rewards, but it's overall kinda meh. Kameos are a fun addition. The gameplay feels good for the most part (aside from issues like P1 advantage, which while resolved now is crazy that it made it out of testing). That's about it. Otherwise, this is an unfinished project that was rushed out by WB and overridden with cash-grabs at every corner. Give it a year and maybe a discount before you check it out, as long as monetization hasn't run totally wild it might be worth it by then.

Straight up downgrade to MK11 if you exclude visuals and core gameplay.

• Story is okay, the ending is bad.
• Customization is lacking.
• Fatal Blows, cut scenes and UI is locked at 30 FPS.
• Invasion Mode is boring.
• Enormous amount of QoL features from MK11 are missing.
• Fatalities are short and lackluster.
• Kameo system is an obvious fan service, and will end up suffering from repetition once NRS stops dropping balance patches.

And here's the funniest part:

• 70 dollars for base game that seems unfinished in every aspect excluding online play.
• 40 dollars for KP that features two characters that should've been in the game to begin with.

Meanwhile SF6:

• 60 dollars for the base game that offers more content and polish.
• 84 dollars for the deluxe edition (15 dollars more than the base version of MK1), and it gives you 4 characters, cosmetics and other things.

Wait for sale or Komplete Edition, until then SF6 is an objectively better game both from casual and competitive perspective.
